tasks.short: Spot service and safety problems, gather facts, and recommend better procedures or training to the manager.

steps.what: Supervisor notices problems: complaints, near misses, slow service, skipped checks
Supervisor gathers guest feedback, incident forms and checklist results

loop.input: Free-text guest comments and near-miss descriptions for the period, with staff names removed.
loop.output: Themes with the comment IDs that support each theme.
loop.check: Each theme must cite at least two comment IDs whose text contains the theme's key words; counts per theme are computed from the IDs, not by the model; quotes must match the source verbatim.
loop.stop: One pass per week; if fewer than ten comments, show the raw list instead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Guests describe the same problem in many different words; a keyword list misses most of them.

steps.what: Supervisor discusses with staff and the chef what goes wrong
Supervisor writes the proposal recommending measures to improve work procedures and safety
Restaurant manager decides which measures to take
Supervisor updates the work instruction and explains it at the briefing

tasks.design: A weekly {BI} view joins guest feedback scores, near-miss and incident forms from a {WORKFLOW} form, digital hygiene checklist results and service times per shift; a bounded model step groups free-text comments into themes tied to comment IDs. A proposal template in {DOCS} pre-fills the facts so the supervisor writes only causes and measures for the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback, incidents and checklists sat in mailboxes, paper and spreadsheets, so building a case took hours.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms and checklists can be digital at no cost, and language models group free-text comments when a check ties themes to sources.
tasks.still_hard: Finding the real cause needs talking to staff; data shows symptoms, not reasons.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a procedure fails in a busy service and getting the team to change habits.

ambition.what: A weekly look at service and safety themes, instead of acting only after a serious complaint.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time collecting facts and more on causes and coaching; the manager decides from consistent proposals.

reach.task: Improve kitchen procedures after near misses
reach.learn: Whether the same near-miss form and themes serve the kitchen.

evidence.claim: Dashboards can join form, checklist and till data per shift.
Systems fit to monitor attendance, behaviour or performance need works council consent in the Netherlands.
AI that monitors and evaluates workers' performance is high-risk; removing staff names and showing shift-level themes keeps this step outside it.

assumptions: Boundary: from noticing a problem to the measure explained to staff; training delivery is outside.

Input contract: guest feedback from the survey tool, near-miss forms filled by staff in the {WORKFLOW} form, hygiene checklists from the digital checklist, service times from the till; fallback is the supervisor's own notes.
Staff names are removed before the theme step; the view shows shifts, not individuals.
Manager time and staff time to fill near-miss forms are outside the supervisor's savings.
unknowns: Whether guest feedback is collected in a structured way today.
Whether staff report near misses at all.
research_questions: Do weekly themes lead to earlier fixes than complaint-driven action?

already_counted.description: Supervisor checks comment themes against a sample of the comments.

incremental.description: Supervisor reminds staff to log near misses and checks the forms are complete.
Staff fill near-miss forms when something almost goes wrong.

approvals.approved_version: The measures as decided by the manager in s5; a different procedure needs a new decision.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where staff rarely log near misses and feedback is mostly spoken, the view stays thin and the supervisor still gathers facts by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan each service: expected covers, portions, production quantities and timing, and who works which station.

steps.what: Supervisor checks bookings and expected covers for the service
Supervisor specifies food portions and plating per course with the chef
Supervisor writes the production plan: quantities, prep times and time sequences
Supervisor assigns workstations and equipment to staff for the shift
Supervisor briefs the team on the plan, timing and stations
Supervisor adjusts the sequence during service when orders pile up

tasks.design: A statistical cover forecast from bookings and till sales history, adjusted by the supervisor, feeds a production plan generator that multiplies covers by the portion specs and prep times held per recipe in the recipe system ({OTHER}) and lays out a prep timeline. Station and equipment assignment stays with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipes, bookings and sales lived apart, so production quantities were estimated from experience in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe tools hold portions and costs per recipe, and forecasting tools let managers adjust a sales forecast and plan from it.
tasks.still_hard: Walk-ins, weather and events move demand; assigning people to stations depends on who is good at what today.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the team and the evening, and changing the plan mid-service without losing the kitchen.

ambition.what: Production quantities set from a forecast for every service, cutting over-production on quiet days.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor adjusts a forecast and a generated plan instead of building them; station choices stay theirs.

reach.task: Set prep lists for the kitchen
reach.learn: Whether the generated prep timeline matches how the kitchen actually works.

evidence.claim: A forecasting tool predicts sales with machine learning; managers adjust it in an app and schedule from it.
In a vendor pilot at four restaurants, the forecast was 25% more accurate, 30% after manager adjustment, and sales per labour hour rose 15%.
A recipe tool rolls ingredient prices up to portion cost per recipe.
Allocating tasks by individual behaviour or traits with AI is high-risk, so station assignment stays a person's call.

assumptions: Boundary: from expected covers to the service running; purchasing is outside.
Input contract: portion size and prep time per recipe, kept by the chef in the recipe system; bookings from the reservation system; sales history from the till; fallback is the spreadsheet plan.
The forecast is statistical, not a staff ranking.
Portion specs change mainly with the menu; daily specification work is for specials.
unknowns: How variable covers are per service.
research_questions: How much food is over-produced on quiet days today?

already_counted.description: Supervisor adjusts the cover forecast for events and weather.
Supervisor checks and adjusts the generated production quantities.

incremental.description: Supervisor reports recipe specs that do not match practice.
Chef keeps portion specs and prep times current in the recipe system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Restaurants with mostly walk-in guests get weak forecasts and keep planning by experience.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count food, liquor, smallware and equipment, explain variances, and report shortages to the manager.

steps.what: Supervisor counts food, liquor and smallware inventories with a count sheet
Supervisor types the counts into the stock spreadsheet
Supervisor compares liquor use with till sales to find variances
Supervisor looks into large variances with bar and kitchen staff
Supervisor e-mails the shortage and breakage list to the manager
Restaurant manager orders replacements from suppliers

tasks.design: Counts go straight into the stock module of the recipe system ({OTHER}) on a tablet, listed by storage location. Expected stock comes from till sales times recipe quantities, including millilitres per drink, so variances per item appear on their own; items below par form a shortage list the supervisor confirms and the manager orders from through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Count sheets, the till and recipes were not linked, so variance meant spreadsheet work after every count.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe and stock tools link to tills and supplier webshops and compute theoretical use from sales.
tasks.still_hard: Counting stays physical; variances from spillage, breakage and staff drinks need a conversation, not a formula.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which variance points to a problem and raising it fairly with the team.

ambition.what: Liquor variances checked weekly per bar instead of monthly, so over-pouring is caught early.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor counts and explains; arithmetic and lists disappear. Ordering stays with the manager.

reach.task: Track bar stock and report shortages
reach.learn: Whether drink recipes in millilitres match how bartenders pour.

evidence.claim: A recipe tool rolls ingredient prices up to portion cost and applies connected suppliers' price changes.
Theoretical usage from till sales times recipe quantities is plain arithmetic in stock tools.
Variance reports per bartender could monitor staff, which needs works council consent in the Netherlands.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock count to shortages reported; ordering and receiving are outside.

Input contract: till sales per item from the till; recipe quantities per dish and drink, kept by the chef and bar lead in the recipe system; par levels set by the restaurant manager; fallback is the count sheet.
Variances are shown per bar or kitchen and period, not per person.
Manager time is outside the supervisor's savings.
unknowns: Whether drink recipes are recorded in millilitres.
How often stock is counted today.
research_questions: What share of liquor variance is explained by spillage versus over-pouring?

already_counted.description: Supervisor confirms the generated shortage list before it goes to the manager.

incremental.description: Supervisor fixes items missing from the count list and corrects mis-scanned counts.
Chef and bar lead keep recipe quantities current; manager keeps par levels current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Kitchens without recipe quantities in the system keep the spreadsheet variance for food, and only liquor is automated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch staff and procedures during service, give feedback, check hygiene routines and write disciplinary write-ups.

steps.what: Supervisor observes workers during service against service and hygiene standards
Supervisor gives feedback on the spot
Supervisor checks hygiene checklists and fridge temperatures on paper lists
Supervisor talks with the employee about a repeated issue
Supervisor completes the disciplinary write-up in the HR template
HR advisor reviews the write-up against policy and law
Supervisor hands the write-up to the employee and files it

tasks.design: Digital hygiene checklists with fridge temperature sensors replace the paper lists, so the supervisor reviews exceptions only. A write-up form in the {HCM} pre-fills employee details, the policy clause and earlier recorded conversations; the supervisor writes the facts, and the HR advisor approves before it is handed over. No model evaluates or writes about staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hygiene records were paper by habit, and write-ups were text documents kept outside the HR system.
tasks.enabler_now: Hygiene codes let businesses choose how they show compliance, and sensor checklists and HR forms are cheap to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Judging people fairly and having the hard conversation stays human; AI evaluation of staff is high-risk and not used.
tasks.human_edge: Being fair, consistent and direct, and knowing when coaching works better than a write-up.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor checks exceptions instead of every paper list; disciplinary rights are unchanged and checked by HR.

reach.learn: Whether sensor alerts cut the time chefs spend on temperature lists.

evidence.claim: A food business may choose how it shows hygiene compliance; records are kept six months, one year for unchilled display.
Food businesses need a HACCP plan, met through the approved hygiene code, and inspectors check records unannounced.
AI that evaluates workers' performance and behaviour is high-risk; this design uses none.
Works councils have consent rights on staff data and on systems fit to monitor behaviour or performance.

assumptions: Boundary: from observing service to the write-up filed; dismissal procedures are outside.

Input contract: checklist items set by the manager from the hygiene code; fridge readings from sensors; earlier conversation records in the {HCM} entered by supervisors; fallback is paper lists and the document template.
Sensor readings are about fridges, not people.
HR advisor time is outside the supervisor's savings.
Input contract for s3: hygiene checks ticked on the kitchen tablet by the cooks on duty, in about the time the paper list takes; fridge readings from sensors kept by the manager.
unknowns: Whether write-ups are stored in the HR system today.
research_questions: How often are paper temperature lists incomplete at inspection?

already_counted.description: Supervisor checks the pre-filled write-up facts and earlier records before submitting.

incremental.description: Supervisor responds to sensor alerts and fixes checklist gaps.
Manager keeps checklist items and sensor thresholds current.

approvals.approved_version: The write-up text as approved by the HR advisor in s6; any change needs a new review.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Sites that rarely write disciplinary notes save only on hygiene lists; observing and coaching stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The supervisor keeps the floor: observing, coaching, assigning stations and adjusting service; spreadsheets, paper lists and fact-gathering shrink.
reach: Chefs' prep lists and hygiene routines
skills_to_grow: Adjusting a forecast with local knowledge
Reading stock variances and raising them fairly
Turning service themes into concrete measures
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who plans every service from a forecast, sees stock and service problems weekly, and spends the time saved coaching the team.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
